develop Partnership
Did you know that software engineers are the most in-demand professionals in the world? Canon Barnett are delighted to have partnered with develop, who are donating STEM toys and resources to introduce children to coding to provide them with early opportunities in tech.
"We are really thrilled to be a part of this amazing project, we feel extremely grateful the develop team reached out to our school. This unique opportunity means that we can carefully plan our curriculum to motivate the pupils to learn about software engineering using high quality stem toys.
I think the vision of develop is very powerful, if the seed is planted early children will feel inspired to learn and this will hopefully direct them to explore their interests further as they move through their educational journey and future career. Our children at Canon Barnett need experiences like this, I am really excited to see where it will take us!"
- Immaculada Matthews, Headteacher

Headteacher: Anita CroftExecutive Headteacher: Sarah Jane Bellerby
After School Clubs
At our school, we’re proud to offer a small but growing range of after-school clubs designed to give children opportunities to explore new interests, develop skills, and have fun beyond the classroom. Our current clubs include a mix of sports and arts and crafts, providing something for both active play and creative expression. These sessions are a great way for children to build confidence, make new friends, and enjoy time together in a relaxed, supportive setting.
We carefully plan our after-school activities to ensure they are inclusive, engaging, and led by enthusiastic staff. Whether it’s learning a new sport, creating something imaginative, or simply trying something different, we want every child to find something they enjoy and look forward to.
We’re always looking for ways to grow and improve our offer, and we’d love to hear from families and children about what clubs they’d like to see in the future. If there’s an interest or talent you’d like us to explore—such as music, dance, languages, or something entirely new—please let us know. We're committed to building a club programme that reflects the interests and passions of our school community.
We are also excited to share that we are currently exploring extended wraparound care in partnership with a trusted local provider. This new provision will offer high-quality care after school until 6pm every day. The extended hours will provide flexibility for working families and give children more opportunities to take part in fun, enriching activities in a familiar setting.
Please contact the School Office to sign up to our clubs this term.

Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is a lovely way for children to start the day. Open to all pupils, it offers a calm, friendly environment where children can enjoy a healthy breakfast and take part in quiet activities before the school day begins. We are also excited to share that we are currently exploring extended wraparound care in partnership with a trusted local provider. This new provision will offer high-quality care after school until 6pm every day. The extended hours will provide flexibility for working families and give children more opportunities to take part in fun, enriching activities in a familiar setting.
As we continue to develop this offer, we’ll keep families updated with more details and how to register interest. We are committed to supporting our families and ensuring that our school is a place where children feel happy, safe, and cared for—from the moment they arrive in the morning to the end of the day.
Please contact the School Office to request a place at our current Breakfast Club.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher: Anita CroftExecutive Headteacher: Sarah Jane Bellerby
Rights Respecting School
We are on our journey to becoming a Rights Respecting School and are working towards our Bronze Accreditation from the UK Committee for UNICEF (UNICEF UK) this year. The Rights Respecting Schools Award places children’s rights at the heart of school policy and practice, strengthen children's sense of belonging and voice even more.
There are four key areas of impact for children at a Rights Respecting school: wellbeing, participation, relationships, and self-esteem. The Award will recognise our achievement in putting the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child into practice within the school and beyond. Children’s knowledge and understanding of their rights, how they and others should be treated, and their sense of self-worth will be developed further. The Rights Respecting Schools Award gives children a powerful language to use to express themselves, to challenge the way they are treated and to challenge injustices for other children. Children will be involved in how the Award is implemented in school, led by our School Council, and will also be involved in decisions about their learning.

PHSE at Mulberry Canon Barnett
For further details please see our Curriculum Overview linked here
At Mulberry Canon Barnett our PHSE teaching aims to help children know and value who they really are and how they relate to other people in this ever-changing world.
We have a whole school approach to the teaching of Personal, Health, Social and Economic education through the use of the Jigsaw scheme of work. There are six puzzles taught across the year, which follow and build upon previous learning. The whole school will be learning about the same topic but at a level that is appropriate to their age.
The units of work are called puzzles and have the following themes:
Each of these topics is launched in a whole school assembly by the subject lead. Throughout the lessons children are encouraged to be aware of their thoughts and feelings and are given opportunities to reflect on their behaviours and attitudes. A variety of games, stories, film clips help to make the learning fun and interesting and our children tell us they really enjoy the lessons.

The extended hours will provide flexibility for working families and give children more opportunities to take part in fun, enriching activities in a familiar setting.
Benefits for Our Families:
As we continue to develop this offer, we’ll keep families updated with more details and how to register interest. We are committed to supporting our families and ensuring that our school is a place where children feel happy, safe, and cared for—from the moment they arrive in the morning to the end of the day.
Please complete the link below to express an interest in Wraparound Care at Mulberry Canon Barnett-this information is incredibly useful to us as we plan for this provision for new and existing families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Nursery - Mulberry Canon Barnett Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher: Anita CroftExecutive Headteacher: Sarah Jane Bellerby
Our Nursery
We are delighted to announce the opening of our new fully funded nursery, offering high-quality early years education for all 3 and 4-year-olds. Our nursery offers a rich, play-based curriculum delivered by experienced early years practitioners who understand the importance of care, creativity, and early learning. We currently have Nursery places available, including 30 hours of fully funded nursery care available to all families. This provision is available to all families, with no cost, and is part of our commitment to giving every child the very best start to their learning journey. Our nursery is a welcoming, nurturing space where children can grow in confidence, curiosity, and independence. Families can choose for their children to attend half days too if they wish.
We are delighted to welcome Ms Clare to our Early Years Team this year. Ms Clare brings a wealth of experience, expertise, energy and enthusiasm! Children enjoy a wide range of activities, both indoors and outdoors, designed to support their social, emotional, and academic development. We focus on building strong relationships, encouraging communication, and helping every child to feel safe, valued, and ready to thrive.
What We Offer:
We believe that the early years are a crucial time in a child’s development, and our nursery provides a safe, stimulating, and joyful environment for children to begin their learning journey.
Why Choose Our Nursery?
We invite you to come and visit our nursery to see firsthand what makes it such a special place for your child’s first steps in learning. Our Early Years Team are always ready to chat with you in greater detail about our provision and how we support every child’s development.
We warmly invite families to come and be part of our school community from the very beginning of their child’s education. Whether families are new to the area or already have older children in school, our nursery is open to all. We have places available, so please get in touch with the school office to arrange a visit or to find out more about how to register your child. We have spaces in other years for those families with older children too. We can’t wait to welcome you.
Please do not hesitate to contact the School Office at any time to talk through the application process. Please just ask if you would prefer to complete the forms with a member of our staff as we would be very happy to help. This can be a daunting process for new families and we are here to help at any time

pageCache.text:
Headteacher: Anita CroftExecutive Headteacher: Sarah Jane Bellerby
Performance
Children at Mulberry Canon Barnett Primary are assessed on an ongoing basis to ensure that we understand where they are with their learning and how best to move them on. This assessment is undertaken by class teachers and support staff through a wide variety of methods such as observations, discussions with children, questioning, marking work, group and independent work, and some routine tests such as spellings and times tables.
In the summer term of each academic year children in specific year groups sit statutory Department of Education tests:
Children in Year 6 sit Key Stage 2 SATs (Standard Assessment Tests) in reading, GPS (Grammar, Punctuation and Spelling) and maths. Where writing is teacher assessed.
At Mulberry Canon Barnett Primary children in year 2 sit:
Optional Key Stage 1 SATs (Standard Assessment Tests) and are assessed in reading, GPS (Grammar, Punctuation and Spelling) writing and maths.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium - Mulberry Canon Barnett Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher: Anita CroftExecutive Headteacher: Sarah Jane Bellerby
Pupil Premium
The staff and governors at Mulberry Canon Barnett are committed to ensuring that all pupils have access to a curriculum that meets their personalised needs in order to achieve at the highest levels possible.
The Pupil Premium is an allocation of funding in addition to the budget provided to schools to support specific groups of pupils who are vulnerable to possible underachievement. These include pupils who are entitled to Free School Meals (FSM) or have been in receipt of FSM within the last six years, those looked after by the LA and the children of armed service personnel. This funding is intended to support us in diminishing the difference in attainment between different groups of pupils.
The total amount of pupil premium funding we received for the 2024 – 2025 year was £121,000
The funding contributed to the success of Mulberry Canon Barnett in the following ways:
Resources to support reading, writing and mathematics.
Throughout the academic year we used this additional money:
This year we are seeking to maintain and improve:
How do we know it is making a difference?
We track the progress of all our pupils in school on a termly basis and more frequently for pupils identified as require additional support and we analyse groups of children and their progress e.g. boys/girls, FSM, Pupil Premium and other characteristics.
